newsitem.title: ITALY: Corruption scandal fugitive returns to Italy.
newsitem.headline: Corruption scandal fugitive returns to Italy.

text.p: Gianfranco Troielli, one of the last major fugitives wanted in the corruption scandals that swept Italy in the early 1990s, returned from abroad on Sunday night and gave himself up to authorities, police said.
Troielli, a former member of the now-defunct Italian Socialist Party, had been at large since 1992.
He was a close friend of former party leader and prime minister Bettino Craxi, who was convicted in four corruption cases and is living in self-imposed exile in Tunisia.
Troielli, who had been living in Kenya, was wanted in connection with bribes paid to political parties in exchange for contracts to build a suburban railway north of Milan.
He was convicted in absentia at a trial earlier this year and sentenced to six years in jail.
According to Italian newspapers, magistrates also suspect he was the mastermind behind a scheme to funnel bribe money paid to the Socialists out of the country and into foreign bank accounts.
The Italian news agency AGI said Craxi sent a fax to media organisations during the night from his exile in Tunisia, saying Troielli had never been entrusted to manage funds for him.
Upon his return to Italy, Troielli was served with the arrest warrant first issued in 1992 and taken to Milan's Opera prison for questioning by magistrates.
Scandals known as Tangentopoli (Bribesville) shook Italy for most of the first part of the decade and led to the fall of the old political order.
The main victims were the parties that had governed the country since the end of World War Two -- particularly the Christian Democrats and the Socialists.
The main charge against a host of politicians and businessmen was violation of laws on the funding of political parties.
In most cases, parties demanded bribes from companies in exchange for public works contracts.
Craxi is the most illustrious figure embroiled in the scandals. The Socialist prime minister from 1983 to 1987 has been sentenced to more than 25 years in jail.
